targetTexts.1: A good name is more desirable than great riches; favor is better than silver and gold.
targetTexts.2: The rich and the poor have this in common: The LORD is Maker of them all.
targetTexts.3: The prudent see danger and take cover, but the simple keep going and suffer the consequences.
targetTexts.4: The rewards of humility and the fear of the LORD are wealth and honor and life.
targetTexts.5: Thorns and snares lie on the path of the perverse; he who guards his soul stays far from them.
targetTexts.6: Train up a child in the way he should go, and when he is old he will not depart from it.
targetTexts.7: The rich rule over the poor, and the borrower is slave to the lender.
targetTexts.8: He who sows injustice will reap disaster, and the rod of his fury will be destroyed.
targetTexts.9: A generous man will be blessed, for he shares his bread with the poor.
targetTexts.10: Drive out the mocker, and conflict will depart; even quarreling and insults will cease.
targetTexts.11: He who loves a pure heart and gracious lips will have the king for a friend.
targetTexts.12: The LORD’s eyes keep watch over knowledge, but He frustrates the words of the faithless.
targetTexts.13: The slacker says, “There is a lion outside! I will be slain in the streets!”
targetTexts.14: The mouth of an adulteress is a deep pit; he who is under the wrath of the LORD will fall into it.
targetTexts.15: Foolishness is bound up in the heart of a child, but the rod of discipline drives it far from him.
targetTexts.16: Oppressing the poor to enrich oneself or giving gifts to the rich will surely lead to poverty.
targetTexts.17: Incline your ear and hear the words of the wise—apply your mind to my knowledge—
targetTexts.18: for it is pleasing when you keep them within you and they are constantly on your lips.
targetTexts.19: So that your trust may be in the LORD, I instruct you today—yes, you.
targetTexts.20: Have I not written for you thirty sayings about counsel and knowledge,
targetTexts.21: to show you true and reliable words, that you may soundly answer those who sent you?
targetTexts.22: Do not rob a poor man because he is poor, and do not crush the afflicted at the gate,
targetTexts.23: for the LORD will take up their case and will plunder those who rob them.
targetTexts.24: Do not make friends with an angry man, and do not associate with a hot-tempered man,
targetTexts.25: or you may learn his ways and entangle yourself in a snare.
targetTexts.26: Do not be one who gives pledges, who puts up security for debts.
targetTexts.27: If you have nothing with which to pay, why should your bed be taken from under you?
targetTexts.28: Do not move an ancient boundary stone which your fathers have placed.
targetTexts.29: Do you see a man skilled in his work? He will be stationed in the presence of kings; he will not stand before obscure men.
